name: Are Roof Coatings a Good Option for Aging Roofs?

mainEntity.name: Are roof coatings a good option for aging roofs in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: Are roof coatings a good option for aging roofs in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Roof coatings can make sense when a roof is aging but still fundamentally sound. They are often used on certain low-slope roofs to help improve water resistance and reflect heat, which can be useful in Los Angeles County. But a coating is not a replacement for a failed roof system. If there is rotten decking, widespread membrane failure, major ponding, or recurring structural movement, the coating will not solve the underlying issue. Before considering this option, have the roof evaluated to confirm that the substrate is dry, stable, and compatible with the coating product. You should also ask how long the coating is expected to last, what maintenance it needs, and how future repairs will be handled. A coating can be a cost-effective bridge strategy in the right situation, but only if the roof is a suitable candidate.
acceptedAnswer.description: Roof coatings can be a good option for some aging roofs if the base roof is still structurally sound and the surface is suitable for coating. They can help reduce leaks and improve reflectivity on certain low-slope systems. Coatings are not a fix for rotten decking, major ponding, or widespread failure.
